title: Coding Challenge 1: Abstraction
description: Learn the principle of Abstraction in Object-Oriented Programming. Abstraction focuses on exposing essential qualities while hiding internal complexity. Create a Human class that models a person with essential properties and behaviors: a 'name' property and a 'run()' method that returns a message.
requirements: The constructor should accept and store a 'name' parameter
Implement a 'run()' method that returns a string
The run() method should return '[name] is running' format
hints: Use the 'class' keyword to define a class
Methods don't need 'function' keyword inside classes
Use template literals or string concatenation for the message

tests.name: Human class exists
tests.test: function() { try { const h = new Human('John'); return typeof h === 'object' ? { success: true } : { success: false, message: 'Human is not a class' }; } catch(e) { return { success: false, message: e.message }; } }

tests.name: Human has name property
tests.test: function() { try { const h = new Human('Alice'); return h.name === 'Alice' ? { success: true } : { success: false, message: 'name property not set correctly' }; } catch(e) { return { success: false, message: e.message }; } }

tests.name: Human has run() method
tests.test: function() { try { const h = new Human('Bob'); return typeof h.run === 'function' ? { success: true } : { success: false, message: 'run() method does not exist' }; } catch(e) { return { success: false, message: e.message }; } }

tests.name: run() returns correct message
tests.test: function() { try { const h = new Human('Charlie'); const result = h.run(); return result === 'Charlie is running' ? { success: true } : { success: false, message: 'Expected "Charlie is running", got "' + result + '"' }; } catch(e) { return { success: false, message: e.message }; } }

tests.name: Works with different names
tests.test: function() { try { const h1 = new Human('Emma'); const h2 = new Human('David'); return h1.run() === 'Emma is running' && h2.run() === 'David is running' ? { success: true } : { success: false, message: 'run() method not working with different names' }; } catch(e) { return { success: false, message: e.message }; } }
